paper.title: A Delphi Study to Strengthen Research-Methods Training in Undergraduate Psychology Programs

claims.text: A two-round modified Delphi with 103 participants (final sample) identified the research-methods skills the UK psychology community deems essential for undergraduates.
Of 78 items included in the consensus process, 38 reached consensus.
Consensus was reached for 34 items; a follow-up survey of 46 heads of department in 2023 furthered the recommendations.
Consensus was not reached for 44 items, spanning advanced analysis techniques, statistics teaching and staff resources.
A qualitative thematic analysis of 707 open-ended text responses yielded two main themes.
A sensitivity analysis requiring 75% essential ratings from all four stakeholder groups changed little.
Ratings were stable across rounds and samples: of 47 items in both rounds, 4 moved to consensus.
Almost 90% of participants rated it essential that students learn to use descriptive statistics before inferential statistics.
The consensus results partially overlap with publicly available curricula: effect sizes and confidence intervals are under-represented.
The study provides open data, summary data sheets and analysis code that allow others to reproduce the analyses.

findings.location: Discussion, Summary of results, p.5 vs bp_work/materials_extract/results/final/0.main_table.csv
findings.evidence: The paper reports 'n items reaching consensus' = 34 items (Discussion, Summary of results, p.5); the authors' own stored output (bp_work/materials_extract/results/final/0.main_table.csv) gives 28. results/table2_verbatim.csv splits them as 26 (Round 1) + 8 (Round 2) = 34, i.e. the Round-1 items appear to be counted twice. Our Python port of manuscript.Rmd also returns 28.
findings.question_for_authors: Is the number of items reaching consensus 28 or 34, and how is the Round-1/Round-2 split counted?

findings.evidence: Paper: median percentage rating items as essential = 74% (IQR 60-86). Stored output over the same 78 items gives median 70.0% (our port: 70.1%, IQR 55.9-85.1).
findings.question_for_authors: Which item set and aggregation produce the reported 74% (IQR 60-86)?

findings.evidence: Random functions used and set.seed() never called.

Rating value 10 encodes 'unable to rate'. In sum_stats() it is set to NA and excluded from the denominator, but in the plotting chunk it is recoded to 0. The paper reports 3% unable to rate without saying which treatment underlies the reported percentages.
findings.question_for_authors: Are 'unable to rate' responses excluded from the denominator or counted as a rating of 0?

findings.location: Methods, Consensus definition, p.3 vs code/manuscript.Rmd:157,322-330
findings.evidence: The paper defines consensus as more than 75% rating an item essential; the code uses perc_essential >= 0.75 (at least 75%). Items sitting exactly at 75.0% would be classified differently.
findings.question_for_authors: Was the preregistered threshold >75% or >=75%?
